To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) cooperation in noisy repeated games is enhanced when intentions are observable, 2) subjects condition exclusively on observable intentions, 3) subjects use simpler strategies than in control games, and 4) subjects use punishment and forgiveness in a manner consistent with the returns to cooperation.

(1) observable intentions lead to more cooperative behavior than unobservable intentions, (2) intentions are more important in noisy games than in control games, (3) subjects use simpler, lower memory strategies, and (4) subjects are tolerant or punitive in noisy games depending on the returns to cooperation.

(i) intentions are a powerful signal in repeated interactions, (ii) intentions can be used in simple ways, and (iii) subjects are tolerant when the returns to cooperative behavior are high, and punitive when the returns are low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the ability to observe intentions influences cooperation in noisy repeated games.
how intentions affect behavior in repeated games.
the role of intentions in social interactions, and we argue that intentions can serve as a mechanism to facilitate cooperation in social interactions, even when intended actions are noisy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
observable intentions lead to higher cooperation, and that subjects use intentions to condition on the actions of others.
observable intentions lead to more efficient cooperation in noisy games, with subjects using simpler, lower memory strategies.
the role of intentions in repeated games with noise is to increase the level of cooperation, but not the degree of punishment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of intentions in noisy repeated games is not to facilitate the implementation of cooperation but to allow subjects to condition on intentions, which leads to more cooperation.
intentions matter, and that the ability to condition exclusively on intentions is a key factor in cooperation.
the role of intentions in repeated interactions is to facilitate cooperation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intentions can play a crucial role in noisy environments, and that the way subjects respond to intentions depends on the relative importance of the costs of cooperation.
intentions are a powerful tool for promoting cooperation in repeated interactions.
the role of intentions in cooperation is not just a theoretical curiosity.
